items.title: 美股每日交易简报 | 2026-11-10
items.summary:
美股每日交易简报 | 2026-11-10
1. 盘面解读
11月9日（周一）大盘强势反弹——SPY收涨+1.45%至$752.69（日内高点$755.42），QQQ涨幅高达+2.52%收于$679.35，IWM+1.83%。这是11月5日（-4.24%）暴跌后的技术修复行情，AI板块领涨（英伟达逆市-4%+为特例），整体情绪倾向Risk-On。然而，今日盘前08:30公布的10月CPI环比0.4%（超预期0.3%），叠加沃勒鹰派表态，纳斯达克100期货盘前已扩大跌幅至-1.5%，美元指数升至102.02，10年期美债收益率拉升至4.901%——Risk-On向Risk-Off骤然切换，今日开盘压力显著。

2. 全球宏观与重磅新闻
按对今日美股盘面影响力排序
🔴【头号催化剂】美国10月CPI超预期，12月加息50bp预期急升
10月CPI环比+0.4%，高于预期+0.3%，前值+0.6%；核心CPI环比+0.3%，高于预期+0.2%，前值+0.3%。受去年10月政府停摆影响，劳工统计局本次不公布同比数据（9月同比为3.7%）。
CPI数据公布后，2至5年期美债收益率当日上涨超10个基点；10年期收益率拉升至4.901%；美元指数短线急升约20点至102.02；现货黄金下挫约30美元至4049.50美元/盎司。
市场影响：通胀连续超预期，直接强化12月FOMC加息预期，交易员已完全消化12月加息25bp，并开始计入50bp可能性。高估值科技/成长股首当其冲，纳斯达克100期货盘前跌幅扩大至-1.5%。伊朗冲突、关税及数据中心建设热潮今年均对通胀形成推升。
🔴【美联储最鹰信号】理事沃勒：若通胀居高不下，12月应加息50bp
沃勒凌晨表态：经济强劲、就业稳定、通胀过高，尤其担忧通胀广泛性；若10月核心CPI超0.3%，应考虑加息50bp；即使通胀改善，也支持加息25bp。明确表示至少需要收回此前三次预防性降息，同时强调"并非超级偏鹰，不想重创经济，不会把利率提高150或200个基点"。
沃勒还指出：货币政策的限制性远没有此前认为的那么强，实际利率须上升才能维持当前限制性。对股市大幅波动，表示通常不影响其利率判断。
市场影响：沃勒为本轮最强鹰派信号的集中释放，CPI数据印证了其加息框架，大幅压缩了12月降息/观望预期，对利率敏感板块（科技、地产、高估值成长）构成直接利空。
🟠【超级IPO】Anthropic冲击美国科技IPO融资纪录，拟募资最高904亿美元
Anthropic拟通过IPO筹集最多644亿美元，发行价区间每股70至78美元，发行8.014亿股，部分股东另出售2360万股；同步推进总计260亿美元私募配售，对象包括AMD、博通、Alphabet旗下谷歌、美光科技、微软、英伟达和台积电。IPO+配售合计最高904亿美元，有望超越SpaceX纪录。
完全摊薄估值约1.4万亿美元，目标市值约1万亿美元。截至10月31日年化营收约810亿美元（较9月环比+100亿美元）；三季度营收接近170亿美元，上年同期仅14亿美元；营收超10万美元客户达11,900家；约250家客户过去12个月营收至少1000万美元。预计因RSU结算产生38亿美元税务义务；总承诺支出约9009亿美元，仅截至2027年9月一年内即有约700亿美元到期。可向博通发行至多420亿美元票据；预计IPO及配售净收益约846亿美元。
市场影响：Anthropic路演本周启动，直接拉升整个AI产业链（NVDA、AMD、MU、MSFT均为配售对象或关联受益方）。同时成为AI基础设施资本支出持续高景气的最强信号之一，对半导体/云计算板块情绪显著提振，但需防范"AI抛售潮后IPO定价能否守住"的不确定性。
🟠【台积电】批准409亿美元资本预算，分别投资Anthropic/OpenAI各5亿美元
台积电董事会核准资本预算约409.27亿美元，用于先进制程、先进封装、成熟/特殊制程产能升级及2027年研发资本预算等。
台积电同时批准以Anthropic IPO发行价投资至多5亿美元普通股，并投资至多5亿美元购买OpenAI优先股，合计至多10亿美元；另宣布将设立专注芯片领域的基金。台积电10月营收同比飙升60%，四季度预期更高。
市场影响：台积电双重利好——CapEx扩产信号强化晶圆代工景气，战略押注Anthropic+OpenAI表明顶层AI算力需求确定性。对半导体产业链（AMD、MU等AI芯片受益方）今日存在情绪拉动，但受CPI超预期压制，需观察开盘后能否守住。
🟠【美伊和谈】布油单日跌近8%，伊朗核谈判重大进展
特朗普在会晤卡塔尔首相后表示"伊朗战争正走向结束"；报道称美伊核谈判就伊朗铀浓缩丰度达成一致，布油盘中跌近8%。今日CPI数据公布后，布油自8月以来首破90美元。
国防部长赫格塞思对弹劾决议强烈回应，称"弹劾是闹剧"，同时表示"超过80%的伊朗核工业基础已不复存在"，"我们控制着霍尔木兹海峡"。美众议员已提交弹劾赫格塞思的决议。
市场影响：油价急跌对能源股（MPC等）构成直接压力，对通胀中期路径产生分歧解读（能源降价有助于后续CPI，但当前数据已超预期）。地缘政治缓和理论上利好Risk-On，但被CPI鹰派信号压制。
🟡【黄仁勋风波】NVDA逆市跌超4%，黄仁勋遭股东集体诉讼
昨日黄仁勋风波持续发酵——美官员称与黄仁勋有婚外情的女子为中国情报机构工作，中国外交部回应"纯属捕风捉影"；黄仁勋今日遭股东集体诉讼，指控涉嫌欺诈。英伟达盘前一度涨超2%后转跌，昨日正式收跌超4%。
市场影响：个股层面，诉讼不确定性压制NVDA短期走势（上周五前收于$178.10）；但Anthropic私募配售中英伟达列名其中，AI需求叙事短期未受根本动摇。两个信号方向相反，NVDA今日走势将成为盘面风向标。
🟡【AI产业链】Anthropic新模型发布；Adobe、IBM/微软、GoodRx多项AI落地
Anthropic发布最强旗舰模型——Fable 5.2多项测试力压GPT-6 Astra，Mythos 5.2均提速并降价，竞争格局对行业整体AI支出预期偏正面。
Adobe在Firefly和Creative Cloud发布新代理和工具，强化AI产品矩阵。
IBM与微软联合推出Imagine企业AI智能体平台，微软提供AI、云和安全基础。对MSFT（$546.81）今日构成额外正面支撑，但受CPI压制，涨幅空间有限。
GoodRx盘前涨超7%，报道称其为谷歌Gemini医疗健康服务的启动合作伙伴。
🟡【软银】两年来首次季度亏损，愿景基金遭AI股大跌重创
软银两年来首次季度亏损，AI股暴跌重创愿景基金，美国数据中心项目遭巨额减值。软银CFO表示认为数据中心延期不会带来直接风险；软银已为美国数据中心业务放缓制定预案，考虑转向其他国家。
市场影响：软银愿景基金折射AI基础设施投资估值压力，对数据中心主题股（ETN $361.73等）构成情绪扰动。
🟡【中国宏观】中国10月CPI/PPI数据，A股ETF连续净流入纪录
中国10月CPI同比增0.7%，数据存储设备涨45.4%；10月PPI同比增5.7%，创2022年6月以来最高。今日中国10月贸易数据将公布，需关注出口数据对全球供应链信号的影响。
A股股票型ETF连续25个交易日净流入，合计超6200亿元，创最长连续净流入纪录。恒指今日收涨0.44%，沪指收涨0.08%，日经225收涨2.9%。
阿里巴巴建议分拆平头哥于香港联交所主板独立上市。智谱拟最多40亿港元回购H股，上限为已发行股份1%。
市场影响：中国PPI强劲反映上游价格压力，输入性通胀风险不可忽视。中国内需数据及贸易数据将影响美国对华出口敏感板块。
🟡【其他要闻】
俄美乌三方会谈：首日会谈结束，将于周三继续，地缘缓和预期对全球Risk-On有边际支撑。
Berkshire Asset Management LLC 13F（三季度）：科技股持仓超其他所有板块；新进埃森哲、CrowdStrike；重仓戴尔科技、摩根大通、艾伯维、微软（$546.81）、苹果（$350.61）；清仓MGM Resorts、Mohawk Industries等；减持思科、麦当劳；对可选消费减持力度最大。
Coursera将裁减约10%全球员工，产生1400万至1700万美元遣散费用，折射非AI科技公司成本压力。
BioNTech以2.05亿美元购买FDA优先审评券。
阿联酋航空总裁表示希望明年获得多达五架波音777X客机，波音订单需求边际改善。
联发科10月销售额550.3亿元台币，同比增长5.77%，半导体上游整体需求保持扩张。
美国10月NFIB中小企业乐观程度指数97.8%，预期98.2%，前值97.9%，略低于预期，显示中小企业信心温和走弱。
ADP数据：截至10月24日过去四周，美国私营部门就业平均每周增加1.975万个，就业市场仍偏强，支持沃勒加息逻辑。
华强北RTX5080价格直降4000元：从10月23日约1.8万元降至约1.4万元，RTX5060微调约200元，英伟达产品终端价格出现调整，需观察对NVDA需求叙事的边际影响。

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: Stanford's century-long AI study admits it's already out of date
items.summary:
Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." The recent retraction of some 1,400 scholarly papers for failure to meet academic standards highlights the urgency of that message. [...] It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress.

The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. items.title: Fall Staff Town Hall highlights ‘human-centered AI,’ community partnerships | Latest | NDWorks | University of Notre Dame
items.summary:
McGreevy highlighted Notre Dame's opportunities to use AI to advance research, particularly through the Data, AI, and Computing Initiative, led by Nitesh Chawla, the Frank M. Freimann Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Lucy Family Director for AI & Academic Strategy, as well as the University’s growing strength in AI ethics, including the work of Meghan Sullivan, the Wilsey Family College Professor of Philosophy and founding director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common [...] From the staff perspective, Cullinan said AI presents opportunities to work more efficiently and better steward the University's resources. But those efforts would remain “human-centered," a dynamic he said might seem contradictory at other universities.

“Not at Notre Dame,” Cullinan said. “I think the most important asset that we have, and will have, is our people.” [...] “What will set our students apart is their competency in interpersonal skills: their ability to make moral judgments, to recognize injustice, and to work on addressing that," he said.

McGreevy echoed Father Dowd's characterization of a "bilingual" education, saying students should still be challenged even as AI makes some assignments easier.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." The recent retraction of some 1,400 scholarly papers for failure to meet academic standards highlights the urgency of that message. [...] It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress.

The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. They want to build an agentic business,” said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting. “Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage.” [...] “AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making and create meaningful value across our business,” said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next. “Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”

items.title: Fall Staff Town Hall highlights ‘human-centered AI,’ community partnerships | Latest | NDWorks | University of Notre Dame
items.summary:
McGreevy highlighted Notre Dame's opportunities to use AI to advance research, particularly through the Data, AI, and Computing Initiative, led by Nitesh Chawla, the Frank M. Freimann Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Lucy Family Director for AI & Academic Strategy, as well as the University’s growing strength in AI ethics, including the work of Meghan Sullivan, the Wilsey Family College Professor of Philosophy and founding director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common [...] From the staff perspective, Cullinan said AI presents opportunities to work more efficiently and better steward the University's resources. But those efforts would remain “human-centered," a dynamic he said might seem contradictory at other universities.

“Not at Notre Dame,” Cullinan said. “I think the most important asset that we have, and will have, is our people.” [...] “What will set our students apart is their competency in interpersonal skills: their ability to make moral judgments, to recognize injustice, and to work on addressing that," he said.

McGreevy echoed Father Dowd's characterization of a "bilingual" education, saying students should still be challenged even as AI makes some assignments easier.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Path Robotics raised $300 million at a $2.45 billion valuation
items.summary:
Path Robotics, which builds programs that guide self-operating factory robots, raised $300 million in a Series E round that puts its valuation at $2.45 billion, according to Bloomberg. The valuation is close to four times its previous level. [...] Founded in 2018, the company has centered its work on its Obsidian physical AI model, which gives robotic arms and quadrupeds the ability to weld upwards of 12 different parts, according to Bloomberg. The model lets robots perceive their surroundings, think through problems and adjust on the fly, rather than executing a fixed set of instructions. [...] Path Robotics has 50 advance orders to deliver for Rove, a welding robot that pairs Boston Dynamics’ Spot quadruped with Path Robotics’ technology, according to Bloomberg. According to the startup, the robot is set to join human welders at shipyards, construction sites and large industrial campuses beginning next year.

Customers include U.S. shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls$HII Industries and Saronic Technologies, a maker of maritime drones and unmanned military ships, according to Bloomberg.

items.title: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
items.summary:
At the center of Path’s technology is Obsidian, a physical AI welding model that uses real-world production data to help robots identify weld joints, plan and execute welds, and adapt to changing conditions, according to the company.

Path recently introduced Rove, a mobile welding system that pairs Obsidian with a four-legged robot. The system is designed to bring welding capabilities directly to a part rather than requiring the work to take place inside a stationary robotic cell. [...] Share

 Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing 

Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)

  

Columbus-based Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation to expand its robotic welding business and bring its artificial intelligence technology to more manufacturing tasks. [...] Path’s expansion targets a production challenge: manufacturers with demand for more products but limited capacity to build them.

The company develops physical AI—technology that enables robots to perceive their surroundings and adapt their actions to changing conditions. Its initial focus has been welding, where variations in parts and joints can make conventional, preprogrammed automation difficult to deploy.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
